content.title: About
content.content: Canadian bacon is a lean cut of pork loin that is cured, smoked, and then cooked. Unlike traditional streaky bacon, it contains far less fat and has a tender, almost ham‑like texture. It is commonly used in breakfasts, salads, and classic North American dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from its popularity in Canada, though it is now produced worldwide.
Traditional Canadian bacon is made from the pork loin, not the belly as with regular bacon.
Before cooking, the meat is usually smoked, giving it a distinctive flavor.
In the United States it is a key component of Eggs Benedict – poached eggs on an English muffin with bacon and hollandaise sauce.
Canadian bacon contains about 10 % fat, compared with roughly 30 % in regular bacon.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Provides roughly 12 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Lower fat content
items.content: Compared with regular bacon, it has less saturated fat, making it a more moderate‑diet choice.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Iron is necessary for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Curing and smoking add significant salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Nitrites and nitrates
items.content: These preservatives used in smoking may be harmful in large amounts.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic or intolerant to pork products.

items.title: Cooking safety
items.content: Undercooked bacon may harbor pathogenic bacteria.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canadian bacon can be pan‑fried, baked, or added to omelets, salads, sandwiches, and pasta dishes. It is often sliced thin and quickly browned to a golden crust. Serve hot or cold depending on the recipe.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at +4 °C for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze in a zip‑lock bag at –18 °C, where it remains good for up to 6 months. Before use, check for off‑odors or discoloration – signs of spoilage.
